encoding_decisions.decision: Unit index type is `Fin q x Fin 4` (block, within-block position), so `n = 4q` is `Fintype.card`, the block embedding `E_ell` is `Sigma`-style coordinate injection, and `G_j^bd = ⨁_ℓ G_{jℓ}` is literally a block-diagonal `Matrix (Fin q x Fin 4) (Fin q x Fin 4) ℝ` that vanishes off the diagonal blocks. Removes all index arithmetic from every direct-sum proof.
encoding_decisions.why: The paper's entire productization argument is a statement about diagonal principal blocks; a product index type makes `[Q]_{ℓr}` a definitional projection.

encoding_decisions.decision: The assignment space is `BlockCode q := Fin q → (Fin 3 x Bool)` (per block: which of the three balanced directions, and its sign), with the decoding `signOf : BlockCode q → (Fin q x Fin 4) → ℝ`, `signOf z (ℓ,u) = (if (z ℓ).2 then 1 else -1) * v ((z ℓ).1) u`. `Z_n` is `Set.range signOf`; a design is a `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.FiniteDesign (BlockCode q)`. `Fintype (BlockCode q)` is automatic, so NO `Fin (6^q)` enumeration is ever needed and arbitrary cross-block dependence is still representable.
encoding_decisions.why: `Z_n ≃ (Fin 3 x Bool)^q` exactly; this is the single decision that makes the exponential-support theorem finitely tractable.

encoding_decisions.decision: The Moore-Penrose radius `xᵀ K† x ≤ 1` is encoded WITHOUT a pseudoinverse: `ass:response-range` is `∃ y, x = K *ᵥ y` and `ass:response-radius` is `∀ y, x = K *ᵥ y → y ⬝ᵥ (K *ᵥ y) ≤ 1`. For PSD `K` and `x ∈ range K` these are exactly `x ∈ range K` and `xᵀ K† x ≤ 1` (if `x = Ky = Ky'` then `y - y' ∈ ker K` so `yᵀKy = y'ᵀKy'`, and `K†x = P_range y`). Mathlib has no Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse for matrices, so this is the faithful pseudoinverse-free form; the sibling run `EXP_DesignPm1ExactnessBoundaryV1_Research` (`twoBlockLaplacianPinv`) had to hand-build a spectral-action pseudoinverse for one fixed matrix, which does not generalize to a menu.
encoding_decisions.why: Avoids building a general Moore-Penrose theory while keeping `def:response-classes` a literal two-atom structure (P2).

encoding_decisions.decision: `λ_max` is a TOTAL function `lambdaMaxPSD (A) := sSup {t | ∃ y, ‖y‖ ≤ 1 ∧ t = y ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ y)}` (no `IsHermitian` argument), with the two bridge lemmas F3 needs: `lambdaMaxPSD A ≤ c ↔ (c • 1 - A).PosSemidef` (the LMI form used in every boxed program) and `lambdaMaxPSD A = hA.eigenvalues.sup'` for Hermitian `A` (the trace/eigenvalue form used by `lem:finite-trace-isotropy`).
encoding_decisions.why: Every boxed program in the paper is stated as an LMI `L ⪯ cI`; a total sSup-Rayleigh definition makes the LMI direction free and confines the spectral theorem to one helper file.

encoding_decisions.decision: Handle nodes (`def:matrix-discrepancy-handle`, `def:heterogeneous-block-local-sdp`) are each ONE `def` returning a bundled record (`MatrixProgramData`, `HetLocalSDPData`), declared as auxiliary non-node structures in the same file. This keeps the one-node-one-`def` mapping while letting the def carry the several objects the core packages into `H_mat` / `H_het`.
encoding_decisions.why: P3 requires a construction definition to be a single `def`; the core's own text calls these 'construction handles' collecting several objects.

Build-inline, `small`-to-`medium`: (i)-(iii) are `Finset` algebra over reused Causalean lemmas; (iv) is the one nontrivial step and is the machinery every later theorem consumes, so it belongs in a Helpers file. lem:finite-trace-isotropy.notes: `λ_max(A) ≥ tr(A)/r` with equality iff `A = (tr A / r) P_K`, for `A = K^{1/2} Q K^{1/2}`, `r = rank K`. Pure linear algebra, no design content, `depends_on = []`. Proof route: `range A ⊆ range K` (since `range K^{1/2} = range K`), the eigenvalues of `A` restricted to `range K` are `r` nonnegative numbers summing to `tr A`, so max ≥ average with equality iff all equal; then `A` vanishes on `range(K)ᗮ`. REUSES `Matrix.IsHermitian.spectral_theorem` / `Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues` (`Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Spectrum`), `Matrix.PosSemidef.sqrt` (`Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Order`) and `Matrix.rank` (`Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Rank`), plus the E-4 bridge `lambdaMaxPSD A = hA.eigenvalues.sup'`. Build-inline, `medium`: the equality case (identifying the restriction with a multiple of the range projector) is the only delicate step and is standard.
